subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Friction at the Atomic Scale
description: A short lesson to help you apply Friction at the Atomic Scale.

hook.text: Zoom in far enough and smooth metal looks like a mountain range.

buildup.text: Tiny peaks called asperities collide, deform, and weld under pressure.

discovery.text: Friction comes from breaking those micro-welds and plowing through peaks.

twist.text: Two perfectly clean metals in a vacuum bond instantly. Too smooth is bad.

climax.text: Engineers polish just enough — too rough wastes energy, too smooth seizes.

punchline.text: Friction hides in the valleys between atoms.

quiz.question: Why can two perfectly smooth metals bond in a vacuum?
options: Magnetic forces pull them together permanently
Without oxide layers or air, surface atoms bond directly
The vacuum creates suction between the surfaces
